title: Quality Gates and Observability Contract for Feature Rollouts
author: Priya Raman
content:
Overview:

This design spec defines a product-level "observability contract" and set of automated quality gates that must be satisfied before, during, and after feature rollouts in Redwood Inference. The intent is to make rollouts predictable, measurable, and reversible by defining the telemetry, thresholds, dashboards, and automated actions owned by product and platform teams.

Goals:
- Create a minimal, standardized telemetry contract for any new routing/serving/optimizer feature that impacts production inference (latency, cost, correctness).
- Define pass/fail quality gates that can be evaluated continuously and used by CI/Release orchestrations and canary controllers.
- Specify required dashboards, alert rules, and remediation playbooks for failed gates.
- Provide a clear owner matrix for who implements telemetry, who validates signals, and who executes rollbacks.

Non‑goals:
- This spec does not mandate implementation detail for instrumentation libraries; it requires observability outputs (metric names, tags, dimensions) and example collectors.
- It is not a replacement for model quality evals or human QA for semantic regressions; it complements those systems.

Background and Motivation:
Redwood supports multiple rollout modes (canary variants, traffic shaping, cost-aware fallbacks) that change the runtime shape (batching, quantization level, kernel selection). In the past 18 months we have observed two classes of rollout issues: (1) subtle latency regressions under tail load caused by changed batching behavior, and (2) cost regressions due to higher-than-expected token mix. These failures were often discovered late because required telemetry was not instrumented consistently.

Contract Summary (high level):
- Required metrics (names are canonical and must be implemented by the service/feature):
  - inference.requests_total{service, model, deployment, variant, route} (counter)
  - inference.tokens_generated_total{service, model, deployment, variant, route} (counter)
  - inference.latency_p50, inference.latency_p90, inference.latency_p99{service, model, deployment, variant, route} (histogram/summary)
  - inference.error_rate{service, model, deployment, variant, route, error_type} (counter)
  - inference.cost_estimated_usd_total{service, model, deployment, variant, tenant} (gauge/counter)
  - inference.cache_hit_ratio{service, model, deployment, variant, route} (gauge)
  - inference.kv_cache_evictions{service, model, deployment, variant} (counter)
  - rollout.health_score{deployment, rollout_id, step} (gauge, 0..100)

- Required distributed traces: a single top-level span that includes the following tags: span.kind, model, variant, route, tenant_id, request_id, request_type, seq_len. Sampling must be sufficient to cover p99 latencies across variants during canaries.

SLOs and Gate Thresholds (example):
| Signal | Gate type | Pass threshold | Advisory threshold | Owner |
|---|---:|---|---|---|
| latency_p99 (route) | hard gate | <= 2500 ms | 2500-3000 ms | platform/serving-runtime |
| error_rate (route) | hard gate | <= 0.5% | 0.5%-1.0% | product/serving-runtime |
| cost_estimated_usd_total (tenanted burst) | soft gate | delta <= +12% | +12% to +20% | finance & product |
| cache_hit_ratio (model) | advisory | >= 85% | 75%-85% | eng-caching |
| rollout.health_score | hard gate | >= 90 | 80-89 | release-automation |

Gate semantics:
- Hard gate: failing a hard gate should pause the automated rollout and trigger an incident if the degradation persists for the evaluation window (default: 15 minutes).
- Soft gate: allows rollouts to continue but must create a ticket in the rollout runbook and notify product owners.
- Advisory: recorded for post‑mortem analysis and not enforced automatically.

Evaluation windows and baselines:
- Default evaluation window: 15 minutes sliding window for canaries, 1 hour for initial A/B experiments.
- Baseline population: all SLOs compare the candidate variant to a baseline fleet percentage (default baseline: previous stable variant at equal traffic mix). For cost signals, the baseline uses a 7‑day rolling average to smooth diurnal traffic.

Telemetry Tagging & Dimensions (required labels):
- service: logical service name (e.g., inference-api, router)
- model: model short id (e.g., llama-2-13B-8k-q4)
- deployment: customer or global deployment id
- variant: rollout variant id (e.g., v2-quantized-canary)
- route: public API route or internal route name
- tenant: tenant id for multi-tenant cost attribution
- rollout_id: unique rollout orchestration id (UUID)

Dashboard & Alerting Requirements:
- Canary dashboard template (required for every rollout) that includes: request rate, latency p50/p90/p99, error rate, cost delta vs baseline, cache hit ratio, kv cache evictions, top 10 endpoints by latency, trace sample waterfall for p99.
- Automated alert runbook rules:
  1) Hard gate breach -> create PagerDuty incident and pause rollout.
  2) Sustained soft gate breach (>= 3 evaluation windows) -> create P1 ticket for product & finance review.
  3) Rollout.health_score drop of >= 15 points in 15 minutes -> trigger rollback.

Automated Actions & Integration Points:
- Canary controller MUST be able to: pause rollout, rollback to previous variant, throttle traffic percentage, and run A/B traffic split based on config. The controller integrates with rollout.health_score and gate evaluations (REST webhook: /rollout/v1/{rollout_id}/actions).
- CI integration: every PR that changes a rollout-affecting component must include a generated telemetry checklist (see Checklist section) and unit tests validating metric emission where feasible.

Telemetry Checklist (example file attached as a template in the repo):
- [ ] All required metrics instrumented with canonical names and tags.
- [ ] Tracing span emitted for request pipeline with required tags.
- [ ] Canary dashboard JSON created from the template and included in PR.
- [ ] Automated gate definitions committed to rollout config (YAML).

Example rollout config snippet (YAML):
```
rollout_id: 8b4f2f2e-3a2b-4f7a-9e2a-9b8c1c7f0d11
name: q4-quantized-performance-canary
target: /api/v1/generate
variants:
  - id: v1-stable
    traffic: 90
  - id: v2-quantized-canary
    traffic: 10
gates:
  - name: latency_p99_route
    type: hard
    operator: lte
    threshold_ms: 2500
    evaluation_window: 15m
  - name: cost_delta_tenant
    type: soft
    operator: lte
    threshold_percent: 12
    baseline_days: 7
```

Observability Implementation Notes (engineering guidance):
- Metric formats: prefer OpenMetrics exposition; tag cardinality must be limited to avoid high-cardinality explosions (see infra-standards metric-cardinality page).
- Trace sampling: use head-based sampling augmented with dynamic p99-targeted burst sampling during canaries.
- Storage retention: canary traces and metric retention should be retained for 90 days. Aggregated SLO windows are retained for 365 days.

Failure Modes and Mitigations:
- Missing metrics: block rollout (hard gate) and mark rollout as telemetry-incomplete; remediation: implement fallback instrumentation shim (provided library) and re-run canary.
- Flaky signals (diurnal spikes): use baseline smoothing and require at least 3 consecutive failing windows before escalating.
- Cost signal noise: pair estimated cost signal with token mix and model selection signals to reduce false positives.

Ownership & RACI (concise):
- Product: defines rollout policy and approves gate thresholds (R/A).
- Platform/Serving Runtime: implements metrics, tracing hooks, and rollout controller integrations (R/C).
- Eng-observability: provides dashboard templates, alerting rules, and SLI computation (R/C).
- Finance: approves cost gates and participates in post-mortems for cost regressions (C).

Rollout Playbook (operational steps to run a canary):
1) Create rollout entry in the Release Manager with rollout_id and attach PRs for telemetry and controller changes.
2) Run smoke tests in staging and ensure telemetry checklist passes.
3) Start canary at 5% traffic for 30 minutes. Observe hard gates for 15m windows.
4) If hard gates pass for 2 consecutive windows, increase to 20% and continue evaluation.
5) If any hard gate fails: pause rollout, run rollback action, and execute incident triage playbook.
6) If soft gates fail: notify product & finance and continue if risk is acceptable; track for 24h before full rollout.

Migration & Backwards Compatibility:
- Existing services must implement the minimal subset of metrics within one quarter of spec publication. New services will be blocked in CI if telemetry is missing.

Roadmap & Next Steps:
- Q2 2027: Publish rollout controller webhook contract and dashboard templates; instrument the top 10 high-traffic routes.
- Q3 2027: Enforce CI blocking for telemetry checklist and provide a telemetry validation tool.
- Q4 2027: Integrate automated cost-attribution with billing to enable per-rollout cost chargeback.

Appendix A — Example Alert JSON (Prometheus Alertmanager rule):
```
groups:
- name: rollout-gates
  rules:
  - alert: RolloutLatencyP99Exceeded
    expr: avg_over_time(inference_latency_p99{route="/api/v1/generate", rollout_id!=""}[15m]) > 2.5
    for: 15m
    labels:
      severity: critical
    annotations:
      summary: "Rollout {{ $labels.rollout_id }} p99 latency exceeded"
```

Appendix B — References and related pages:
- See /product-docs/requirements/quality-aware-quantization-rollout-prd-2026-12-01 for model-quality integration notes.
- See /eng-platform/dashboards-and-alerts/canary-dashboard-templates for dashboard JSON templates.
